I definitely do still see it as a mistake since Garrett or I would’ve adamantly said not to play the golden rod since we for sure had the numbers and knew it, yall didn’t trust us enough to tell us that which i’d still mostly credit Carlee for. Not to say that AK is completely undeserving, but on the basis that he predominantly survived that tribal due to others actions and not his own, and then just rode out the game on the tails of that alliance that he couldn’t flip on again since everyone else voted for him… i’m just not seeing it compared to Ale and Cass

Specifically on the point of being fluid and not sticking to one side, I think you can absolutely bend your game in whichever way you want - but you gotta play the cards you’re dealt to a degree if you want to win. Carlee played the perfect example of as much of a fluid game you can play with how this season went - she had cross alliance connections that wound up feeding her vital information to nearly make it to the end, but she knew she could never fully jump to the other side or else it would torch her game. (i’m not trying to bash you I just need to bring up the opposite example) On the other hand, you attempted to play the fluid game but it just ended up playing to your detriment since they used that info to chip away until only their alliance was left. In your case, it would’ve been less fun to play the alliance based game - but you would’ve had an exponentially better shot at winning. So, I don’t feel naturally inclined to vote for AK just since he was the most fluid of the three, I think it served Ale and Cass best to be less fluid with their allies
